question: to the Commission Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Estrella Galán (The Left), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Elisabetta Gualmini (Renew), Murielle Laurent (S&D), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Merja Kyllönen (The Left), Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE), Per Clausen (The Left), Ignazio Roberto Marino (Verts/ALE), Damien Carême (The Left), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Erik Marquardt (Verts/ALE), Danilo Della Valle (The Left), Ilaria Salis (The Left), Giuseppe Lupo (S&D), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Rima Hassan (The Left), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Brando Benifei (S&D), Annalisa Corrado (S&D), Pasquale Tridico (The Left) Subject:

Following the meeting in Brussels with family members of some of the victims of the Cutro shipwreck which occurred in late February 2023, accountability and measures to prevent such tragedies are still lacking in Italy and at European level. At least 94 people drowned in Italian territorial waters near Steccato di Cutro, Calabria, as the vessel sank just metres from the Italian shoreline. At the time, the government had restricted the response to maritime distress calls involving migrants. While not an isolated case, this tragedy is significant as it could have been prevented. Moreover, it highlights the lack of rights afforded to the family members of the deceased and leaves both the families and the deceased as victims of this tragedy. Therefore, we ask: 1.
Is the Commission ready to establish a clear framework for providing both psychological and legal support to the families of those who died in the Mediterranean Sea?
Will the Commission consider opening a humanitarian corridor to Europe for the victims’ family members to enable them to be present for potential legal proceedings?
Will the Commission ask the Italian Government to provide concrete support for the families and ensure accountability for what happened in February 2023 as it had promised?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.9.2026) The Commission deeply regrets the tragic loss of lives in the shipwreck off Cutro in February 2023. Rendering assistance to persons in distress at sea is a duty and an obligation under international law for the Member States. Migrant deaths at sea underline the need for a comprehensive approach to migration management and the fight against migrant smuggling. Under international maritime law, responsibility for coordinating search and rescue operations lies primarily with the competent national authorities. It is for the competent national authorities, including judicial authorities where appropriate, to establish the facts and assess compliance with the applicable legal framework. The Commission continues to monitor developments within the limits of its competences under the Treaties. The Commission has no competence to request an independent assessment of an individual search and rescue operation carried out by a Member State. The Commission continues to support Member States in strengthening search and rescue, including through the Search and Rescue Contact Group, which brings together Member States, EU agencies to exchange operational experience and support the effective implementation of the applicable legal framework. The Victims’ Rights Directive1, revised in 20262, provides for a comprehensive set of rights for victims of crime and their family members3. It is for national authorities to ensure their application in the circumstances raised by the Honourable Members, in line also with the principle of access to justice under Article 47 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU4. The examination and issuance of visas fall within the competence of the Member States, as laid down in applicable EU law.

1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2012/29/oj/eng. 2 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2026/1472/oj. 3 In its role of Guardian of the Treaties, the Commission closely monitors the transposition and implementation
of these rules by the Member States. 4 Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union [2012] OJ C326/391, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/treaty/char_2012/oj.
